based_on: 23 tracked accounts — 7 direct rivals, 8 content creators, 7 international benchmarks, 1 platform; 11 with live post-level data this week

patterns.title: News-peg reels are what's working, and IFM's own view counts now prove it
patterns.text: IFM now has real view counts for all 37 reels. In the last 30 days the top 3 of 15 reels were all news pegs: Tata Sons IPO (13,700 views), the Tata boardroom story (2,887) and the NSE IPO (2,044). The median reel got 1,048. Anushka Rathod's one countable post this week was also a news-decoded reel (20K likes). Make one news-peg reel a week a fixed slot rather than something that happens when there's time.

patterns.title: Pinned hits still flatter the big accounts. Measured on current posts, IFM leads.
patterns.text: CA Rachana Ranade's headline is 46.4K likes, but her 3 September posts average 1,461 (32x lower). For Vinita it's 583 against 16 (36x). Using current posts only, IFM gets 35 likes on 535 followers (6.5%). Anushka gets 2.0% on her one countable post, Her Money Talks 0.33%, LXME 0.27%, Rachana 0.15% and Monika Halan 0.1%. Read avg_likes_recent, not avg_likes.

patterns.title: A third account now hides its likes, so views and growth have to carry the tracker
patterns.text: Shreyaa Kapoor hides likes on 6 of 6 posts for the third week. Ellevest hides them on 4 of its 5 own posts. New this week: Anushka Rathod, the biggest account in the set, hides them on 2 of her 3 September posts. That makes 3 of the 11 scraped handles partly or wholly unmeasurable, up from 2. IFM's own reporting has already moved to views. The Competitors tab should do the same and switch to follower growth and cadence before likes stop working as a measure.

patterns.title: Posting more doesn't help without a hook, and not even LXME's reels are landing
patterns.text: Her Money Talks posted 6 times between 19 and 27 Sep and averaged 12 likes (0.33%). Monika Halan posted 5 times between 20 and 27 Sep and averaged 23 likes on 21K followers. The surprise this week is LXME, a High-threat account: its two latest reels got 10 and 51 likes, while its static posts got 1,041 and 544. Posting often and choosing reels both fail without a reason to stop scrolling. That supports putting IFM's effort into hooks and news pegs rather than volume.

patterns.title: The gap is still open: nobody targets mums and nobody makes games
patterns.text: All 23 accounts were checked again. None targets mums specifically, and none runs an interactive game. The two accounts closest to IFM's model, Her Money Talks and Dhan Diksha, are still small on Instagram. Female Invest's Playvest is the only practice tool in the set, and it's only available inside a paid subscription. Stock Rush, the live quizzes and Mutual Fund Manager are still unmatched, so each reel that routes viewers to a game is using an advantage no other account has.
